microtheory.name: visual_cognition
microtheory.definition: Higher-level visual processing — attention, mental rotation, visual imagery, visual reasoning, change blindness. The interface between vision + cognition. Substrate analogue: substrate's high-level visual processing on top of feature extraction.

concepts.name: selective_visual_attention
concepts.definition: Choosing what subset to process. Spatial vs feature vs object-based. Substrate analogue: substrate's drive-priority on visual concepts.

concepts.name: spatial_attention
concepts.definition: Attending to a spatial location. Posner 1980 cueing paradigm. Substrate analogue: substrate's location-conditioned activation.

concepts.name: feature_based_attention
concepts.definition: Attending to a specific feature (color, motion, orientation) wherever it appears. Substrate analogue: substrate's feature-conditioned activation.

concepts.name: object_based_attention
concepts.definition: Attending to an object as unit. Substrate analogue: substrate's Concept-conditioned activation.

concepts.name: covert_attention
concepts.definition: Attention without eye movement. Mental shift. Substrate analogue: substrate's σ-shift without input change.

concepts.name: inattentional_blindness
concepts.definition: Missing salient events outside attention. Simons + Chabris gorilla. Substrate analogue: substrate's attention-gated processing.

concepts.name: change_blindness
concepts.definition: Missing changes across views. Especially with intervening masks. Substrate analogue: substrate's change-without-attention failure.

concepts.name: attentional_blink
concepts.definition: Brief inability to detect 2nd target ~500ms after 1st. Refractory period of attention. Substrate analogue: substrate's attention-cycle limit.

concepts.name: repetition_blindness
concepts.definition: Missing 2nd instance of repeated stimulus. Substrate analogue: substrate's identity-suppression mechanism.

concepts.name: visual_imagery
concepts.definition: Internal visual representation. Activates similar brain regions to perception. Kosslyn 1980. Substrate analogue: substrate's runtime visual simulation.

concepts.name: mental_rotation
concepts.definition: Rotating mental image. Time linear in angle. Shepard + Metzler 1971. Substrate analogue: substrate's geometric transformation.

concepts.name: image_scanning
concepts.definition: Scanning mental image takes time proportional to distance. Substrate analogue: substrate's spatial-traversal cost.

concepts.name: imagery_perception_neural_overlap
concepts.definition: fMRI shows imagery activates ventral visual cortex similarly to perception. Substrate analogue: substrate's shared imagery-perception mechanism.

concepts.name: visual_working_memory
concepts.definition: Maintain visual info actively. Capacity ~4 objects, Luck + Vogel 1997. Substrate analogue: substrate's persistent σ for visual concepts.

concepts.name: iconic_memory
concepts.definition: Brief (<1s) sensory store of visual input. Sperling 1960. Substrate analogue: substrate's brief input buffer.

concepts.name: long_term_visual_memory
concepts.definition: Standing 1973 — humans recall 10000+ pictures with >90% accuracy. Substrate analogue: substrate's large visual Concept repertoire.

concepts.name: visual_search
concepts.definition: Finding target among distractors. Feature search (fast, parallel) vs conjunction search (slow, serial). Treisman. Substrate analogue: substrate's search-time as function of distractor count.

concepts.name: pop_out
concepts.definition: Target with unique feature pops out regardless of distractor count. Substrate analogue: substrate's parallel feature-detection.

concepts.name: salience_map
concepts.definition: Topographic map of attention-attracting strength. Itti + Koch 1998. Substrate analogue: substrate's spatial-attention prior.

concepts.name: mental_models_visual
concepts.definition: Internal models supporting reasoning about spatial layouts. Johnson-Laird 1983. Substrate analogue: substrate's internal spatial Mt.

concepts.name: perspective_taking
concepts.definition: Imagining a different viewpoint. Substrate analogue: substrate's viewpoint-transformation.

concepts.name: visual_reasoning
concepts.definition: Solving problems using visual representations. Geometric proofs, mechanical thinking. Substrate analogue: substrate's spatial-Term evaluation.

concepts.name: visual_illusions
concepts.definition: Mismatches between physical stimulus + perception. Reveal underlying processes. Substrate analogue: substrate's failure-mode probes.

concepts.name: muller_lyer_illusion
concepts.definition: Lines with outward arrows appear longer than with inward. Possibly size-constancy misapplied. Substrate analogue: substrate's misapplied prior.

concepts.name: ames_room
concepts.definition: Distorted room appears rectangular from special viewpoint; figures appear different sizes. Substrate analogue: substrate's prior overriding sense data.

concepts.name: ponzo_illusion
concepts.definition: Same lines appear different sizes against converging perspective lines. Substrate analogue: substrate's depth-cue-modulated size.

rules.name: attention_gates_conscious_perception
rules.head: the substrate processes a complex scene
rules.body: only attended subset reaches conscious access. Unattended content can produce inattentional blindness. Substrate's attention-gated processing.

rules.name: feature_search_is_parallel_conjunction_search_is_serial
rules.head: the substrate searches for visual target
rules.body: if target differs by single feature, search is parallel (pop-out). Conjunction targets require serial scan. Treisman.

rules.name: mental_rotation_takes_linear_time_in_angle
rules.head: the substrate rotates a mental image
rules.body: the time is proportional to the angle of rotation. Shepard + Metzler 1971. Substrate's geometric-transformation cost.

rules.name: visual_working_memory_limited_to_few_objects
rules.head: the substrate maintains visual items actively
rules.body: capacity is ~4 objects, regardless of features per object. Luck + Vogel 1997. Substrate's persistent-σ capacity.

rules.name: illusions_reveal_underlying_processes
rules.head: the substrate experiences a visual illusion
rules.body: the failure reveals which processes are actively contributing — size constancy, depth cues, lateral inhibition. Substrate's mechanism-revealing failure modes.
